title: Top Eats & Drinks
subtitle: Don't leave Spain without these — one drink and three foods per city.

drink.name: Horchata con fartons
drink.detail: Sweet tiger-nut milk with pastry sticks for dunking. Try Horchatería Daniel or any chuferia near the beach.

foods.name: Paella Valenciana
foods.detail: The original — chicken, rabbit, green beans. Not seafood. Casa Carmela May 28 ✅

foods.name: Clóchinas
foods.detail: Local mussels — peak season May/June. Beach chiringuitos or Mercado Central.

foods.name: Fideuà
foods.detail: Short noodles cooked paella-style in the pan. Same vibe, different carb.

drink.name: Cava
drink.detail: Catalan sparkling wine — say cava, not champagne. Can Paixano or El Xampanyet for standing-room-only vibes.

foods.name: Pan con tomate
foods.detail: Bread rubbed with tomato, olive oil, salt. Every meal starts here.

foods.name: Patatas bravas
foods.detail: Fried potatoes + spicy sauce. Every bar claims theirs is best — compare on the tapas tour.

foods.name: Jamón ibérico
foods.detail: Cured ham carved to order. La Boqueria or any good tapas bar.

drink.name: Vermut (vermouth on tap)
drink.detail: Madrid's Sunday ritual — vermouth with an olive, simple tapas. Casa Alberto or any old bar in La Latina.

foods.name: Churros con chocolate
foods.detail: San Ginés — open 24 hours. Thick chocolate for dipping. Perfect post-wedding recovery.

foods.name: Bocadillo de calamares
foods.detail: Fried squid sandwich near Plaza Mayor. Sounds weird. Trust the locals.

foods.name: Tortilla española
foods.detail: Runny-center potato omelet. Juana la Loca on Cava Baja is the move.
